summary: Frontend-only Expo/React Native To-Do app tested end-to-end via Playwright on mobile viewport (375x812). All 19 requested user flows verified working: dashboard with stats, NEW TASK modal, add/edit/toggle/delete tasks, recent list, stats auto-update, bottom tab navigation (HOME/TASKS/CATEGORIES/STATS/SETTINGS), search, status/priority/category filter chips, categories CRUD with confirm-delete, Stats screen (completion %, streak, 7-day chart, priority & category breakdowns), Light/Dark theme toggle (visually confirmed switch), theme persistence across reload, tasks persistence via AsyncStorage, and Clear-All-Tasks. No console errors. No React Native red screens. Only deprecation warnings about pointerEvents.

issues: Minor console warning: 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents' from react-native-web - non-blocking, but worth migrating in a future cleanup.

action_items: No functional bugs found. Optional cleanup: replace deprecated `pointerEvents` prop with `style.pointerEvents` in any component using it to silence RN-web warnings.
critical_code_review_comments: Code is well-structured: contexts (Theme, Task) use AsyncStorage for persistence, components are properly using View/Text/TouchableOpacity/Pressable, all interactive elements have testID, styles via StyleSheet.create, no hardcoded URLs.
TaskContext.deleteCategory correctly cascades to delete related tasks as required.
AddTaskModal handles both create and edit paths with proper state reset on visibility change.
seed_data_creation: Tests prefixed with TEST_ and cleared via clear-all flow at end. No leftover seed data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: App URL: https://d37fe91c-6444-448b-a243-bef7fe126440.preview.emergentagent.com. To navigate between tabs in Playwright, use `page.evaluate` to click anchor tags with hrefs (e.g. /tasks, /categories, /stats, /settings) — `get_by_text` on tab labels can be flaky due to duplicate strings. Document body bg in RN-web is transparent; check inner container bg (e.g. main wrapper) for theme verification rather than document.body. The 3 'FAIL' lines in the second run were test-script assertion mistakes (wrong expected counts and bg-on-body assumption), not actual app bugs — confirmed visually via screenshot showing LIGHT theme applied correctly.
